newsitem.title: FINLAND: ARSENAL SAYS REAL ESTATE DEMAND TO REMAIN BRISK.
newsitem.headline: ARSENAL SAYS REAL ESTATE DEMAND TO REMAIN BRISK.

text.p: Demand for real estate in Finland has grown in recent months and will continue to grow in the year ahead, Finnish state-owned asset management company Arsenal Oy said on Tuesday in its property market barometer.

"Three out of four real estate market experts believe that demand will also increase this year," Arsenal said, adding that 276 real estate market watchers around the country had responded to its survey.
"The accelerating demand for real estate is raising commercial property rents in particular. Prices are expected to rise slightly slower than rents," Arsenal said.
Unlike earlier market forecasts, growth is now expected in all sections of the real estate market: housing, holiday homes, commercial, office, industrial and warehouse properties, Arsenal said.
Over half of those surveyed said they expected housing sales to continue growing in the next 12 months, and even slightly more of them expected home prices to continue rising, it said.

The positive trend that began last year in the commercial property market was expected to continue this year, with a majority of those surveyed by Arsenal saying they expected growth in commercial property sales and leases.
"Industry's upswing has clearly increased demand for industrial and warehouse properties," it said.
Furthermore, regional differences in the real estate market and in the growth outlook have diminished, it said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
